s1.syndrome_frame: Acute bleeding syndrome with splenic involvement and severe thrombocytopenia
salient_findings: Bleeding from the mouth, nose, and skin
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
One-month history of bleeding
Splenic mass detected two weeks prior to presentation
No prior medical history
Spleen not palpable on examination
Severe thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 1 × 10^9/L
Thrombocytopenia did not respond to recombinant human thrombopoietin, intravenous immunoglobulin, or methylprednisolone
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scan showed splenomegaly with a 57 × 58 mm patchy low-density lesion
Lesion exhibited moderate peripheral enhancement and central hypoenhancement in the arterial phase
Lesion showed slightly reduced enhancement centrally in the venous phase

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a splenic mass, severe thrombocytopenia, and bleeding from multiple sites, along with the imaging characteristics of the splenic lesion, are consistent with lymphoma involving the spleen.

rejected.label: Hairy cell leukemia
rejected.why: While hairy cell leukemia can cause splenomegaly and thrombocytopenia, the lack of specific diagnostic findings such as hairy cells in the bone marrow or spleen makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Splenotic myeloma
rejected.why: There is no mention of plasma cell dyscrasia or other findings typical of myeloma, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Splenomegaly with myelofibrosis
rejected.why: Myelofibrosis typically presents with bone marrow fibrosis and other cytopenias, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Chronic myeloid leukemia
rejected.why: CML typically presents with leukocytosis and other specific findings such as the Philadelphia chromosome, which are not mentioned in the case.

gold: Inflammatory pseudotumor-like follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
